answer: Before an agent may vote or take epoch fees, it must deposit a refundable bond into a shared lagoon and can recover it only after finishing three time-staggered settlements, each routed through a different, randomly assigned karst channel and cleared by an unaffiliated counterparty. If keys later share a controller or treasury, an ember mark is published on the whole set and every bond is slashed. A clone factory then pays in locked capital, delay, and correlated loss, which grows linearly with the number of fake names.
